The '''''Stalker''''' was an [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] under the command of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Akal Zed]].

==History==
[[File:ImpStarDestroyer-TSS.png|thumb|left|250px|''Stalker'']]
The ''Stalker'' was originally assigned to search the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] for new worlds to subjugate,<ref name="CCG-Hoth">{{CCG|set=Hoth Limited|cardname=''Stalker''}}</ref> and would later become part of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Villis Andal|Andal's]] fleet patrolling the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]].<ref name="OE" /><ref name="PG3" />

It would later be reassigned as part of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], his personal [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] that searched for the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters and, more specifically for Vader, the location of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="BtM" />

Eight months after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the ship [[Battle of the Poln system|fought]] [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]]'s forces in the [[Poln system/Legends|Poln system]] as part of [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]].<ref name="CoO">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref>

During Vader's post-[[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Yavin]] search for Skywalker, the ''Stalker'' was one of the ships responsible for launching thousands of [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]] into the far reaches of space to search for the Rebels' new base.<ref name="BtM" /><ref name="CCG-Hoth" /> Alongside another Star Destroyer, the ''[[Avenger/Legends|Avenger]]'',<ref name="Atlas" /> ''Stalker'' launched probes to the [[Allyuen system/Legends|Allyuen]], [[Tokmia system/Legends|Tokmia]], [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth]], and myriad other star systems.<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> One of the droids of this operation successfully located [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the ice [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Soon thereafter, the ''Stalker'' joined Death Squadron in its blockade of the planet during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. As the Rebellion's escape [[Transport/Legends|transports]] attempted to run the blockade, the ''Stalker'' helped to disable at least one of the fugitive [[Starship/Legends|ships]], the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], the final transport to evacuate Hoth.<ref name="CCL">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=''Bright Hope''}}</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the ''Stalker'' participated in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="BtM" /> As part of Death Squadron, the ship survived the battle. Captain Zed refused to obey the new fleet commander, [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], and decided to return to the Elrood sector with his ship.<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The identity of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] that launched the Hoth probe droid has been inconsistent across different [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources. "[[Freedom's Winter]]," the first episode of the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|the radio dramatization of ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] ([[1983]]), includes a scene between Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]] and a subordinate to indicate that Needa's ship, the [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']], launched the probe droid that went on to discover Echo Base.<ref name="Freedom's Winter>{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref> This dialogue was cut from some versions.<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' ([[1989]]) follows the radio drama and says that the droid was launched from the ''Avenger''. However, the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]] ([[1996]]) contradicted this, introducing the ''Stalker'' and identifying it as the ship that launched the droid. The PC program ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' ([[1998]]) and ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' ([[2004]]) followed the card game and name the ''Stalker''. ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' (also 1998) followed the radio drama and Galaxy Guide in identifying the ''Avenger''. Attempting to clarify the discrepancy, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]) states that both ships were responsible for deploying probe droids without stating which ship is seen in the film.<ref name="Atlas" />
